tldr: AFLOW automates agentic workflow discovery for LLMs by formulating it as a search problem over code-represented workflows, using Monte Carlo Tree Search with LLM-driven expansion and execution feedback to iteratively optimize workflows with minimal human intervention.
contributions: Problem formulation generalizing prior workflow optimization approaches as specific cases
AFLOW: an MCTS-based framework that automatically discovers effective workflows across multiple domains
Extensive evaluation on six benchmarks showing AFLOW outperforms manually designed methods by 5.7% and surpasses existing automated approaches by 19.5%
methods: AFLOW represents workflows as LLM-invoking nodes connected by code-based edges and explores the search space using Monte Carlo Tree Search. The framework introduces operators as predefined reusable node combinations (e.g., Ensemble, Review & Revise) to enhance search efficiency. Key components include a soft mixed-probability selection strategy combining uniform and score-based distributions, LLM-driven node expansion using past experience, direct execution evaluation on a validation set, and tree-structured backpropagation of optimization experience to avoid information loss from token accumulation.
results: AFLOW achieves a 5.7% average improvement over state-of-the-art baselines and surpasses existing automated approaches by 19.5% across six benchmarks: HumanEval, MBPP, MATH, GSM8K, HotPotQA, and DROP. Workflows generated by AFLOW enable smaller LLMs to outperform GPT-4o on specific tasks at 4.55% of its inference cost.
limitations: The framework focuses primarily on reasoning tasks with numerical evaluation functions. The search space was simplified by fixing key parameters such as model, temperature, and output format to improve efficiency. Previous linear heuristic search methods like ADAS struggle to generate effective workflows within limited iterations, motivating the MCTS approach.
